Thought: Let me analyze the proton NMR spectrum to identify the different types of chemically equivalent hydrogens:

1. δ 1.20 (d, 3H) - A doublet representing a methyl group
2. δ 2.85 (d, 2H) - A doublet representing a methylene group
3. δ 3.09 (qdd, 1H) - A complex multiplet representing a single proton
4. δ 3.81 (s, 3H) - A singlet representing a methoxy group
5. δ 7.15 (ddd, 2H) - Two equivalent aromatic protons
6. δ 7.92 (ddd, 2H) - Two equivalent aromatic protons

Each of these signals represents a different chemical environment. Counting them up:
1. Methyl group protons (1.20 ppm)
2. Methylene protons (2.85 ppm)
3. Single proton (3.09 ppm)
4. Methoxy protons (3.81 ppm)
5. First set of equivalent aromatic protons (7.15 ppm)
6. Second set of equivalent aromatic protons (7.92 ppm)
Final Answer: 6
